U3: CI build to create Docker images
U4: Documentation for Mesos/Marathon deployment

- YAML-based configuration
- Docker containerization

- Single developer performing all work
- Spring XD as the base platform
- Standard development environment available
- No major architecture changes needed
- Docker is the primary deployment mechanism

technical_and_design_decisions: Use Spring XD as the base platform with the existing module/component model for new source modules (U7).
Use YAML-based configuration files (e.g., servers.yml) for runtime properties, consistent with existing XD conventions (U8).
Adopt Docker as the primary deployment artifact format; provide a Dockerfile and image build conventions (U1, U3).
Use Zookeeper-based service discovery (already used by Spring XD) as the default mechanism (U2).
Implement data partitioning using Spring XD's existing PartitionSelector/MessageBus capabilities, with RDBMS column-based partitioning (U6).
Use HDFS client libraries (hadoop-client) and XD's source module SPI to implement the HDFS source (U7).
Treat Spring Boot upgrade evaluation (U5) as an investigation spike plus prototype to identify breaking changes, not a full upgrade commit.
Treat Mesos/Marathon documentation (U4) as a deliverable document with example configurations; no new code beyond example artifacts.
Target Java 17+ consistent with Spring Framework 6.0 baseline noted in the specification.
assumptions: A single developer (me) performs all activities; no team coordination overhead is included.
Spring XD source, build system, and CI infrastructure already exist and are available.
External services (Rabbit, Redis, Zookeeper, Hadoop, Mongo) are reachable during development for testing.
Hadoop/HDFS cluster is available in the dev/test environment for U7 development and testing.
No new data store or third-party service must be licensed or procured.
Estimates cover only development, not operations or production deployment support.
Unit and integration test infrastructure already exists; effort covers writing tests, not building test frameworks.
Spring Boot upgrade evaluation (U5) assumes a target minor version is provided; effort covers diff analysis and prototype validation.
U4 documentation assumes the underlying Mesos/Marathon XD cluster support already exists; effort covers writing/structuring the guide.
Effort for cross-cutting concerns (refactoring, code review, bug fixing) is captured in a dedicated activity rather than spread across feature activities.

activities.activity_description: Review all 8 user stories, clarify acceptance criteria, define high-level architecture and module boundaries, and produce a brief design note covering Docker configuration, service discovery, partitioning, HDFS source, and configuration property changes.

activities.activity_name: U1: Docker XD Container external service configuration
activities.activity_description: Implement Docker container configuration support including link/binding attributes and environment variables to connect to Rabbit, Redis, Zookeeper, Hadoop, Mongo, etc. Update Docker templates/configuration files accordingly.

activities.activity_name: U2: Service Discovery for Docker XD Containers
activities.activity_description: Integrate service discovery mechanism (Zookeeper-based) so Docker containers can locate and communicate with cluster processes and services. Add discovery configuration options to container deployment descriptors.

activities.activity_name: U3: CI build pipeline for Docker images
activities.activity_description: Configure CI build (e.g., Jenkins) to produce Docker images containing all required components/configurations, run tests inside the image, and publish images to a registry for deployment to multiple environments.
Author a deployment guide covering XD cluster deployment on Mesos with the Marathon Framework, including cluster topology, container definitions, networking, and example Marathon application JSON.

activities.activity_name: U5: Spring Boot dependency upgrade evaluation
activities.activity_description: Investigate applicable Spring Boot version, run upgrade against XD, identify breaking changes, deprecations, and side effects. Produce an evaluation report with findings and recommendations (no full upgrade commitment).

activities.activity_name: U6: Data partitioning strategy (RDBMS to HDFS)
activities.activity_description: Implement a user-supplied partitioning strategy for parallel ingest from RDBMS into HDFS. Add configuration to select a partition strategy (e.g., column-based) and integrate it with the existing RDBMS source and HDFS sink/job pipeline.
Design and implement a new HDFS source module that reads files from HDFS, supports options for path, format, polling, and integration with XD's message bus. Includes module descriptor and packaging.
Add a configurable commit-interval property in servers.yml and wire it into all out-of-the-box jobs that support partitioning, replacing the hard-coded default with the configured value.
Write unit tests for new and modified code: container configuration parsing, service discovery wiring, partitioning strategy, HDFS source module behavior, and commit-interval property handling.

End-to-end integration tests covering Docker image build/run with linked services, service discovery resolution, partitioned RDBMS-to-HDFS ingest, HDFS source ingestion, and commit-interval behavior in a job.
Update/author reference documentation for new properties, the HDFS source module, partitioning strategy usage, and Docker/service discovery configuration examples. Update release notes.

activities.activity_name: Code review, refactoring, and bug fixing
activities.activity_description: Self-review, refactor for consistency and quality, fix issues found during unit/integration testing, and address any regressions uncovered while implementing the user stories.
